x: They were mostly adverts for sofas
f: Steve: "Who is planning their film and TV watching this early?" Ricky's party excuse: "It's to be confirmed, but I can just say this - I won't be at the party".
ex: But when they bring them out this early, you open it, and you think "oh I want to see what films are on" and stuff, and you open it, and about half of the listings are "to be confirmed". It's an utter waste of time, but it's like, who is…
Yeah, 3 weeks in advance, going "Oh I'd better not make any...", well unless it's an amazing thing on telly...
"Are you coming to our party? We've got one, Friday 29th", "Err, I dunno, I've got to watch something on the TV, there's a good film", "What is it?", "Not been confirmed yet, but I'm just..."
"It's to be confirmed, but I can just say this - I won't be at the party", yeah.

q: Steve was livid that Ricky saw Bowie without him. What did he threaten if Ricky went to a secret gig without him again?
a: There'd be no more "Office"
x: He'd tell Jane about the Ritz crackers
f: Steve: "I'm not joking... That's like textbook example of friendship." Ricky's excuse was that Steve was away. Or asleep.
ex: I’ll tell you this. Seriously, if I find out that you do- that you’ve gone to some secret gig or something in the future and I find out- Seriously, that’s it. There’s no more “Office”, there’s no more--
No, I’m not joking. I’m not mucking around, cause that, to me, is like- that’s what friendship is. That’s like textbook example of friendship.

q: Mocking Karl's birthday gloves for Suzanne, Steve asked whether they had his name sewn in them and what else?
a: A piece of string running over the back of his duffle coat
x: A matching bobble hat with a pom-pom
A price tag still on from Woolworths
A free mint tucked in each thumb
f: Steve was treating them as school-kid gloves on a string. Karl's defence was the same as always: "It's what she wanted."
ex: I've told ya before about buyin' presents, it's- it's--
Do those gloves have your name sewn in them?
And a piece of string... that ran over the back of your duffle coat?

q: Karl described the bison on 'The Mammals': a really big hairy head, sort of bald at the back. What did Steve say it sounded like?
a: Someone Karl went to school with
x: A mop left out in the rain
Ricky first thing in the morning
f: Steve: "It sounds like someone you went to school with." Ricky's follow-up: "Was there two of 'em?"
ex: Sort of, bald at the back--
It sounds like someone you went to school with.

q: In Steve's childhood story, what did a kid who lived near him do to a bird that had been run over?
a: Kissed it, thinking that was the Kiss of Life
x: Gave it a burial at sea
Tried to post it to the RSPCA
Fed it a worm to perk it up
f: Ricky first thought Steve meant a girl. The boy "just thought you could kiss something and that would bring it back to life."
ex: I always remember there was this kid who lived near me once, and this bird got run over, and he rushed to it and said “I can save it” and he kissed it. Cause he though he could give it the Kiss of Life.
I thought you meant it was a girl.
He thought he could give it the Kiss of Life, but he didn’t know what the Kiss of Life was, he just thought you could kiss something and that would bring it back to life.

q: In Steve's university story, what was the cleaning lady doing in his room when he came back?
a: Clomping round in his Dr. Martens doing an impression of him
x: Reading his diary to the whole corridor
Using his shoes as plant pots
f: Steve has size 14 feet. Ricky: "I love the fact that she's more popular than you."
ex: And erm, so I was working hard to try and seem kind of cool and not freakish and erm, I came back from studies once and I came in and there's a little old cleaning lady that kind of would always come in every day and clean up our Halls of…
That that's my door's open and I'm not. But I'm not in there and there's people staring in the door and I looked in and the little cleaning lady had my Dr. Martens on and was clomping around.
Making them all laugh, doing an impression of me.
Imagine that! Imagine the psychological scars that has.
I love the fact that she's more popular than you.

q: Steve wondered why the Greeks picked a horse as their gift. What other enormous thing did he suggest they could have hidden inside?
a: A quiche
f: Steve: "We could bake an enormous quiche, be inside that. We could have an enormous soap-on-a-rope."
ex: But in terms of it as an idea initially, I mean, we're gonna give them a gift. Well what should we do? We could bake an enormous quiche, be inside that. We could have an enormous soap-on-a-rope as a- It's the fact that it's an enormous…

...enormous wooden horse as a gift anyway... I don't know if this was a- a popular gift at the time. But it's also the stupidity of the Trojans saying, "Brilliant! I've always wanted an enormous wooden horse. Well what we gonna do with it?…

q: Steve griped that a whole cast made Ricky's show, but only Ricky got invited to dinner with Bowie. Who else went, to Steve's disgust?
a: Ricky's girlfriend, who wasn't even in the show
f: Steve: "Once again, she could have stayed at home." Ricky: "And you could have gone in her place?" Steve: "Hello?"
ex: And the woman, what do you know, who wasn’t involved with the show.
Well, we’re partners. You’ve got to, you know, that’s it. It’s-it’s--
Well, yeah, but once again, she could have stayed at home.
And you could have gone in her place?

q: In Steve's tribe story, a man killed and ate someone from another village. How many pigs did it take to make up for it?
a: Five
f: One pig wasn't enough. "So five pigs apparently made up for the fact that they'd killed one of them." The widow then had to move in with the killer.
ex: They couldn't plug it in. They had an absolute nightmare. But there was one guy, okay? Now, he said that his brother was dying. This was a couple of years ago, right? His brother was dying. He said to his dying brother, "What happened? Why…
Hang on, who are they giving these pigs to? The tribe?

To the tribe of the bloke who he killed and ate. So five pigs apparently made up for the fact that they'd killed one of them. They said, "Well, hang on, what are you gonna, what are you gonna do with this bloke's wife?"

q: Steve described how Karl must picture scientists making a mammoth: they take an elephant and cover it with what?
a: Carpet tiles
f: Karl had pictured them giving the mammoth "the electric shock" to wake it up, which Ricky put down to Frankenstein.
ex: In his head they've got - they've got an elephant, they've sort of - they've had - They put some carpet tiles over it, -
- and they're trying to bring that back to life a a mammoth.

q: Steve's friend with zero street-cred saw a police car driving behind them. What did he say?
a: "Eh up, the pigs, watch it."
f: He followed it with "Just play it cool, play it cool." Steve: "like what I'm supposed to think... you're part of Grand Theft Auto III".
ex: I've never – what? It was, I'll tell ya what almost annoys me almost as much as that, there was a guy I used to know who'd pretend and this guy was like, he'd never done anything wrong in his life, he had no street-cred whatsoever and I…
Like, like what I'm supposed to think what, you've done some crime, you're part of Grand Theft Auto III and we, I better be careful, cos you've got some knocked out – off gear in the back.
“Just play it cool, play it cool.”

q: Steve's idea of a 'useful' wedding DJ announcement asked eight-year-old boys in tiny tuxedos to do what?
a: Slide across the dance floor on their knees
f: "...until they are taken home and put to bed early." Ricky's version called "the overweight aunt in the purple dress" to the floor.
ex: They should do useful things at a wedding. Like, uhm-
[smooth DJ voice] "Will the overweight aunt in the purple dress please now take the floor with a little unfortunate kid...
"As the dance floor is currently empty, will any eight-year-old boys wearing those tiny tuxedos please slide across the dance floor on their knees...
...until they are taken home and put to bed early."

q: Steve's grandad was given false teeth during the war. What state are they in now?
a: Most teeth have come off the wooden plate, leaving about four
x: They've been carved entirely out of wood
They're held in with string and glue
He swapped them with his wife's by mistake
f: "He's got a set of false teeth that make him look like he needs false teeth." His grandmother is "working with about three or four teeth".
ex: Uhm, my grandfather had false teeth given to him during the war.
Well it wa- it was plastic teeth on a wooden pallet, right? That sits at the top of the mouth. He's still got the wooden pallet, but most of the teeth have come off.
So there's about four teeth left. Four--
Four false teeth. He's got four- he's got a set of false teeth that make him look like he needs false teeth.

q: Ricky prowled round the ring staring his opponent out. Because of his beer belly, who did Steve say he looked like?
a: Johnny Vegas getting ready to box
x: Bernard Manning getting ready to box
Big Daddy getting ready to box
Brian Blessed getting ready to box
f: Steve says Ricky was "staring Bovey out and staring the crowd out" while carrying "this ludicrous beer belly".
ex: Well you- he was, kind of, prowling
Round the ring, staring every- you know, staring Bovey out and staring the crowd out.
Rarrrgh! And kind of looking really 'arrrrgh!'
But- but of course he's got this ludicrous beer belly.
D'you know what I mean? So it looks like, it looks like Johnny Vegas is ready to start boxing.

q: As Ricky and Karl got nostalgic about shops being shut on Sundays, what did Steve sarcastically chip in with?
a: "Do you remember space hoppers?"
f: Karl had been remembering getting up early for bread before the shop shut. Ricky's reply to Steve: "Yeah. yeah, shut up."
ex: Uh, it's good because I remember I used to have to get up early to go and get some bread if we didn't have any in, because the shop would only be open for a couple of hours in the morning, whereas now -
Yeah, i remember that. i remember that. shops shut. and you couldn't get aspirin and stuff, certain things...
Exactly, nightmare on a sunday afternoon
Yeah that's right, yeah, pubs didn't open til 12 did they?
Oh, do you remember space hoppers?
Yeah. yeah, shut up. can i ask you something?

q: On Steve's family coach trip back from Paris, what happened to the family who refused to go into the roadside restaurant?
a: They were locked in the coach
x: They were left at the side of the road
They were charged double for their sandwiches
They were made to dress as Butlins redcoats
f: They'd brought sandwiches and just wanted the port. Steve "looked back and just saw this kid with his face pressed up against the glass."
ex: Yeah, they stitched you up. Well I remember we were on a-it was a family trip to France once, we went to Paris. We got the coach, coming back from Paris to one of the ferries, one of the ports, Calais or wherever it was. Coach trip, that's…
"Take me with you. I want to go in the restaurant". They were just stuck in there, I mean, absolutely livid, as you would be.

q: Introducing an "old school" track for his hip hop feature, Steve was asked how he spells "school". His answer?
a: With a K
f: Steve: "Going back in time, rewinding the past." The track was by Digital Underground, the group Steve said featured Tupac Shakur when he first began.
ex: I’m playing an old school track this week, Rick.
Going back in time, rewinding the past.

q: Steve revealed Jonathan Ross had phoned Ricky for advice on clothes. Which look did Steve say Ricky was "goin' for"?
a: The man down the DSS look
f: Steve also asked whether Ricky had "a single pair of trousers that aren't elasticated at the waist." Ross: "I like that look".
ex: I love the fact, you were on the phone to Gervais last night, weren’t you, asking his advice,
He’s goin’ for the man down the DSS look!
I like that look – no, it’s a nice look!
Have you got a single pair of trousers that aren’t elasticated at the waist.

q: Steve's new feature, Songs I'd Like to Play on the Radio, used a burned CD from a friend. Whose name and hometown did Steve give out for the police?
a: Dave Greenwood, from Nottingham
f: Steve: "I would not encourage anyone to make copies of anything for anyone, it is against the law." Ricky: "His name again, if the police are listening?"
ex: Dave Greenwood, obviously breaking several copyright laws there.
I would not encourage anyone to make copies of anything for anyone, it is against the law.
His name again, if the police are listening?
How dare he, how dare he!
...I can give details. It sickens me Rick.

q: Steve said a pub greeted Ricky with "your usual table, Ricky?" Calling him Godfather, what did Steve ask if Ricky could arrange?
a: To have someone iced
x: A free round for the table
f: Ricky explained his sudden power: "I got Polaroid's of all the head of all the stations."
ex: Drop some tickets around now has to go rehearse the show. I was out with you last night went into this pub like we been to a few times before. This guy came in and said your usual table Ricky?
Your usual table? Can I just ask you two questions Godfather? One is, have we won a prize tonight? Two, can you have someone iced for me?
It’s ludicrous, what do you suddenly got over all these people? When did you suddenly become the daddy?
Well I came from nowhere, and y’know, I got Polaroid’s of all the head of all the stations. Yeah, exactly.

q: Ricky banished Steve from the bed to a tiny hotel box chair for the whole England match. Why was Steve especially furious?
a: It was his own hotel room
x: He'd paid for the whole minibar
The chair faced away from the telly
Ricky had eaten all the room service
f: "It's 90 bloody minutes plus the intermission. It was my room. I was furious." At his size, "those tiny little crappy hotel box chairs are no good."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The World Cup · 2010
ex: No, big man. And so I just thought, let's pop the pillows down. That wasn't enough. I said, Steve, I can't do this. I can't watch football with a man on a bed. I said, so go in the chair.
And he sat in this chair!
So I sat in the chair which is, if you're a man of my size, those tiny little crappy hotel box chairs are no good. It's 90 bloody minutes plus the intermission. It was my room. I was furious.

q: Why does Steve flick straight past interviews with Ricky when he's reading the paper on the Tube?
a: In case a bloke says, "Oh, reading about your mate, are you?"
x: Ricky always takes credit for his jokes
He can't face Ricky's photo before lunch
He gets jealous of Ricky's photo shoots
f: Steve dreads the commuter going "Oh reading about your mate, are you?" and "Don't get enough of him. Do you?"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The World Cup · 2010
ex: If I'm on the tube and I'm flipping through the paper, sometimes there'll be an interview with you that I'm not aware is going to be in the paper and I have to flip on by because I don't want a bloke on the tube going, "Oh reading about…
"Don't get enough of him. Do you?" Do you know what i mean?

q: After Karl refused a kidney to the cheeky little kid, who did Steve reveal the kid went on to become?
a: Winston Churchill
f: Karl took the credit anyway: "Maybe I helped. It's like Darren Campbell all over again. I made him stronger."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The World Cup · 2010
ex: Hey, wait. Do you know who that kid went on to become?
Right. Well, maybe I helped. It's like Darren Campbell all over again. I made him stronger. I was tough with him. He saw how tough the world is.

q: Someone bid £50 for Ricky's drawing of Karl in an XFM charity auction. What had Steve done with the bid?
a: Deleted it, thinking someone was winding them up
x: Read it out on air as a joke
f: Karl: "You deleted it?" Steve: "You didn't keep me informed!" Ricky: "He's a buffoon, Karl, isn't he?"
ex: Cause I-I’ve read, I’ve read something- I think there’s been a bid of at least fifty pounds, which is pretty--
I swear to God! I just saw it earlier. I deleted it cause I thought someone was winding us up.
Well, I didn’t know, did I? I didn't reali-You didn’t keep me informed!
He’s a buffoon, Karl, isn’t he? I think, I think you’re an idiot, but sometimes…

q: Steve remembered a commemorative Cliff Richard plate. What did its slogan promise?
a: Cliff never ages, and neither will this
x: A living doll for your wall
The plate the Bachelor Boy chose
f: Ricky imagined a buyer saying "I've married Cliff Richard" and being told "It's a plate." Steve added: "I sleep with it!"
ex: There was one, I think it was Cliff Richard. It was a commemorative plate of Cliff Richard.
It said - it said "Cliff never ages". (chuckling) "Cliff never ages and neither will this."
Really, did it say that? (doing voices) "Tell your friends and - tell them you've married Cliff Richard." "Look, I've married -" "It's a plate." "It's not a plate!"

q: When Karl began a point with "if you go into a toffee shop", which film did Steve say Karl must be living in?
a: Shrek
f: Ricky had already placed him "in a Dickens tale, in the 19th century." Steve later added that Karl had "just come from the candlestick maker."
ex: Where are you going to find a toffee shop?
You're in- you're in a fairy tale.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. You're in a Dickens tale, in- in the 19th century.
Yeah and you go into a toffee shop-
What's your point? You go into a toffee shop.

q: Steve said his anxiety dreams used to be about running to get to school on time, but with his feet running in what?
a: Treacle
f: Ricky said he hadn't had an anxiety dream "for years and years and years". His verdict: "Dunno. Don't care."
ex: Have you had one, Steve? An anxiety dream?
Anxiety dreams? I do have them periodically, yeah. Used to be a lot of things like running to get to school on time, but suddenly your feet are running in treacle and you can her the school bell--
I haven’t had them for years. I just haven’t had an anxiety dream for years and years and years. Yeah, dunno. Don’t care.

Well no, you just genuinely don’t care about anything this is the problem. You’ve just got to a point now where nothing bothers you. It’s like you’re too lazy and disinterested in anything: this show; your career; my career; Karl’s--

q: After Karl left for Cornwall, Ricky predicted the locals would make him King. Steve compared it to the Ewoks in Return of the Jedi elevating which character because he could speak their language?
a: C-3PO
f: Ricky reckoned "the mayor is probably an animal" and "the townsfolk think like Karl", so Karl would "stay there and be made King".
ex: Because I think one, the mayor is probably an animal. --
And I imagine the townsfolk think like Karl.
Do you know what I mean? I imagine he’ll probably, he’ll stay there and be made King
Have you ever seen Return of the Jedi?
In Return of the Jedi, the Ewoks, the little furry creaturs, they see C3PEO and because he can talk and he can speak the language they actually elevate him--

q: Steve has never mastered his front crawl. What did he ask a strong swimmer at his local gym pool?
a: To watch him do his front crawl and tell him if he was going wrong
x: To race him over a couple of lengths
To swap lanes because he was too splashy
f: Steve: "It's only as I was saying it, did I realize what it sounded like." Ricky pointed out they were both in Speedos.
ex: --you've got to breathe at the right moment. And um, I'm in the swimming pool in the local gym...and there's a guy bombing up and down, really doing a great forward stroke. So I...waited till he came up and sort of went, "Uh, excuse me…
Why did you do that, why would you go to a man--
I know! And that was why-that was the problem. It's only as I was saying it, did I realize what it sounded like. "I've just been watching you--
--"swimming up and down, I was really impressed."

q: Playing along with Karl's 'world too heavy' worry, Steve claimed Atlantis proved it. Why did he say Atlantis sank?
a: Its king kept ordering stuff by mail order
x: It kept all its gold in one corner
f: Ricky chipped in that the king bought "Carpets, a lot of carpets" and "all the myrrh, that the wise men didn't want."
ex: Right and what happened is they just kept buying stuff in, mail order. They just kept ordering stuff, like the king and stuff- just kept ordering stuff in mail order. He brought girls across, you know-
Carpets he kept buying, TV se- big screen TV's and stuff like that and eventually-
He bought up all the myrrh, that the wise men didn't want.
Yeah he just- cos he's from like olden times, and he just kept buying stuff, crazy, like he was just a shopaholic basically.
And he was ludicrous, it was li- an- and in the end it was too heavy and it just sunk.

q: Steve once watched Footloose in America. How did he describe the film?
a: Like a film about humans made by aliens who'd only watched our TV and films
x: Like a pop video that goes on for two hours
Like a public information film about dancing
Like a school play with a Hollywood budget
f: Ricky summed up the plot as "That famous film about where- where dancing was banned." Steve called it "an extraordinary film."
ex: But who would get Kenny Loggins then? If the- if the clue was good, who would get Kenny Log- What did he do? Footloose?
That famous film about where- where dancing was banned.

That's an extraordinary film. I saw it once in America. Like you say, Kevin Bacon, in a town where dancing has been banned. I was watching it. It was like if aliens had been watching earth but only monitoring us through our tv and films.
And then tried to make a film about humans. That's the film they'd end up with.

q: Karl didn't make his point to jellyfish expert Vicky because it might have confused her. Finish Steve's reply: "Well, she's a scientist..."
a: "...she's easily confused."
f: Karl had held back because raising it "would have took her off and confused her".
ex: No, but the turtle thing, you know, if you get rid of 'em then the turtles, you know, won't have anything to eat... But, when she said that, I mean, I couldn't say it cuz it would have took her off and confused her but, like--
Well, she's a scientist, she's easily confused.

q: For listeners who've never seen Karl, Steve said he looks a bit like which children's TV character?
a: Mr. Spoon from Button Moon
f: Ricky agreed straight away ("He does! He does!") and added that Karl is the missing link: "half human, half monkey."
ex: Yeah. Well for those that have never seen Karl, I actually, if you remember, I think he looks a little bit like Mr. Spoon from Button Moon.
If you've ever seen that show--

And also he looks like, you know when they say they find a little four-foot human and it's actually half a million years old and they give it a name. It's the first you know, Australopithecus into, right? He looks like one of them as well.
Perfectly round little, he's the missing link. He looks half human, half monkey.

q: Steve claims he's only ever taken one sick day. What was it for, and where did he recover?
a: Tonsillitis, at his mum and dad's
x: Flu, in a hotel XFM paid for
A bad back, on Ricky's sofa
f: Karl: "Is that when you went home, stayed with your mam and dad?" Steve: "Nursed back to health - yeah, got a loving family. So sue me."
ex: Yeah I don't think I've ever taken a day off sick
Except when I that terrible, terrible, terrible tonsillitis.
Is that when you went home, stayed with your mam and dad?
Why's that a problem? Nursed back to health.
No I'm not saying it's a problem-

q: Karl revealed that his leggings-wearing neighbour used to work on 'one of those sex line things'. What did Steve ask?
a: "What was she, an engineer?"
x: "Did she do a discount for neighbours?"
"Did she wear the leggings for it?"
f: Karl carried on regardless: "The weird thing with her was, erm, she had... big eyelids."
ex: She used to wear them and that's what I remembered when I read this piece. She used to work on one of those sex line things.

q: Steve praised the St John Ambulance volunteers at festivals. When did he predict the fat lad with the satchel would finally get off with a girl?
a: When he's giving her mouth-to-mouth
x: When he turns 50 and buys a sports car
When he joins a rock band
When he swaps the satchel for a rucksack
f: Steve: "He's never gonna get off with a girl probably until he's like 30." Ricky: "Did you join the Saint Johns Ambulance last week to get some birds?"
ex: I pointed him out to my-I said, see that fat one over there? In the uniform.
With the glasses and the hair brushed forward.
With the glasses- hair brushed forward, the kind of blue navy jumper.
Little satchel, yeah. He's never gonna get off with a girl probably until he's like 30 and even then its-
And even then it's because he's giving mouth-to-mouth to her...

q: At university, Steve found a cashpoint with someone's card still in it and the PIN already entered. What did he press 'just to check'?
a: Balance, to see how much they had
x: Cancel, to give the card back
Change PIN, to teach them a lesson
f: "It was a considerable sum of money... It was not typical student debt." Ricky imagined the options on the screen: "Steal or go to heaven?"
ex: This is like the Marie Celeste. I went to a cash point but I thought “I can’t get my card in here”. So I realised there was already somebody’s card in the machine, they’d put the code in, but, um, but they-they-they-they disappeared…
Um, I pressed ‘Balance’ just to check what their balance was.
It was a considerable sum of money. I’m not going to lie to you. It was not typical student debt. It was, like, I think they were a foreign student, there was a lot of cash in there.

q: After Karl called him tight with money, Ricky asked Steve if he'd ever splashed out on a lady. What did Steve say?
a: No, but he hoped to one day
x: Yes, but she paid him back
f: Steve to Karl: "I've got no reason to splash money out on you." As for ladies, he's saving it for "The right lady."
ex: I’ve got no reason to splash money out on you--
I’ve never seen you splash money out--
Well, you’ve never been out with me--
(laughing)Have you ever, Steve, have you ever splashed out on a lady?
Um, no, but I hope to one day--

q: Steve said Ricky keeps turning up on lists of ideal dinner guests. What was Steve's first objection?
a: There'd be nothing left to go round for anyone else
x: He'd only talk about The Office
He'd laugh at his own jokes all night
He'd leave before the cheese board
f: Ricky didn't help his case: "And I'm always early." People think he'd be witty, Steve said, but "he'd just be stuffing his face for two hours."
ex: The number of times I've seen you on one of those. The ideal dinner guest.
Not the ideal dinner guest. Well, firstly, there'd be nothing else to go around for anyone else.
So by the time anyone. That'd be it. Yeah. Yeah. The ideal dinner is as long as he comes halfway through the meal.
And I think they mean, oh, it'd be funny because he'd be very witty and charming. No, he'd just be stuffing his face for two hours.

q: As a boy, Steve learned a rude word at school, thinking it was just a stronger 'twit'. What happened when he used it at home?
a: His dad didn't know what it meant either and started calling Steve's mum it
x: His mum washed his mouth out with soap
His dad grounded him until Christmas
His nan started saying it at bingo
f: Steve: "my dad didn't know what it meant either… So he started using it as well!" He's never told him, and wonders whether to this Christmas.
ex: And, uhm… and so I started using this at home ‘cause I didn’t realize what it meant. I started using this at home, “Oh, you twit, you’re a twit,” and saying it to my dad, “You’re a twit, you’re a t—,” you know… but not saying “twit.”
And my dad didn’t know what it meant either.
Which I couldn’t believe. So he started using it as well! Right? So then we’ll be driving in the car, he’d be saying to my mum, “You stupid twit…”

q: Looking back on 2005, Steve said the only time he'd prayed for a natural disaster of Biblical proportions was while watching what?
a: Celebrity Love Island
f: "And it never happened." Ricky added that the only big wind on the island came from Rebecca Loos.
ex: It's been terrible. Well, we've had the, obviously Hurricane Katrina and the tsunami and the earthquake and things, and, um, and it's obviously been terrible and we don't want to be, to be flippant about that. But the only time I was…

And it, and it never happened. And some of the dregs of humanity on that show. I mean I don't know if you saw it, but Paul Danan is a joy because he's a mental case. And I'm saying that, I don't know if that's libelous but, I mean, if…

q: Steve said Karl had muddled up the story of the mountain piano. Where was it really found, according to Steve?
a: On a moor in Scotland
